sections.h2: What sets a Royal Oak house sale apart?
sections.html:
Sellers here deal with the city's Assessing and Building divisions and the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and one variable is whether the house is a registered rental. An owner-occupied house needs the deed, the transfer affidavits and the tax steps, while a rental adds city registration and inspection rules.

This Oakland County suburb lies roughly 10 miles north of downtown Detroit on the Woodward Corridor, with I-75 and I-696 close by. A survey party named it in 1819 for a large oak tree, and it incorporated as a village in 1891 and again as a city in 1921. Royal Oak calls itself the city of trees, and the National Arbor Day Foundation has recognized it as a Tree City USA every year since 1976.

sections.h2: What draws buyers to Royal Oak?
sections.html:
The downtown is among the largest in the Detroit suburbs, and buyers notice how close a house sits to it. Since the late 1990s the blocks along Main Street and Washington Avenue have turned into a dining and entertainment district, with condominium and loft buildings adding residents.

  • Most of the Detroit Zoo lies in Royal Oak, with a portion reaching into Huntington Woods.
  • Corewell Health William Beaumont University Hospital is among the city's listed points of interest.
  • The Royal Oak Music Theatre, the Baldwin Theatre and a comedy club bring evening crowds.
  • Arts, Beats and Eats fills downtown over Labor Day weekend, and the city sponsors events around the Woodward Dream Cruise.
  • The Farmers Market began in 1925 and now stands at 11 Mile Road and Troy Street.

Buyers touring houses near downtown tend to ask about noise, parking and event traffic, so describe event weekends honestly.

sections.h2: Where did Royal Oak's trees and the Red Run come from?
sections.html:
The city grew up around a small river, the Red Run. During the 1930s a WPA project filled in the stretch beside Vinsetta Boulevard, which had been built with the stream as its median, and in 1967 and 1968 the rest of the river inside Oakland County was buried in a six-foot drain pipe. Extensive tree planting since the 1930s earned Royal Oak its nickname, though recent development has sparked arguments over how the urban forest is maintained.

For a seller, the practical point is the mature canopy. Older streets with large trees are part of what buyers picture when they search here, so photograph the yard in full leaf.

sections.h2: What is the housing picture in Royal Oak?
sections.html:
Per capita income reaches $66,293 and household income $101,109 at the midpoint. Federal figures for 2020 to 2024 put the middle owner-occupied home at $328,700, owners in 68.0 percent of homes and rent at $1,381.

Households are small. The average has 1.98 people, 42.3 percent of 2020 households were one person, and only 14.8 percent of residents are minors. Some 82.8 percent kept the same address for a year, and 64.1 percent of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree or more.

An estimated 57,583 people lived here in July 2025, 1.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base. The 1970 count of 86,238 was the peak, and numbers have hovered near 57,000 to 58,000 since 2010. On 11.79 square miles that is about 4,937 people per square mile, so a listing competes with many similar blocks and presentation matters.

sections.h2: Which public school districts cover Royal Oak?
sections.html:
Royal Oak Schools teach most children, though a portion of the city's land is zoned to Berkley Public Schools, so confirm your address before listing. Enrollment decline led the district to merge its two high schools, Dondero and Kimball, into Royal Oak High School in 2006, and its two middle schools into one in 2007.

Private options include schools tied to the Shrine of the Little Flower parish, and a branch of Oakland Community College sits in the city. Families will ask about the district boundary first.

sections.h2: What must a Royal Oak rental owner handle?
sections.html:
Registration with the city comes before any tenant moves in, and the Building Division inspects residential rental units under the Property Maintenance Code. The city's guide tells owners to name a responsible party within 30 miles, post the address inside the unit, respect occupancy limits and keep smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and extinguishers working.

Short-term rentals also need insurance and must hand guests the city's Good Neighbor Policy. A buyer will want to see the registration paperwork, and an unregistered rental is a problem to fix before closing. Penalties escalate with each violation:

Royal Oak rental ordinance penalties by offense, from the city's registration guide
ViolationPenalty
FirstCivil fine of at least $200 plus costs
SecondCivil fine of at least $350 plus costs
ThirdMisdemeanor, fine up to $500, up to 90 days in jail, or both, and registration may be revoked

Questions go to the Building Division at building@romi.gov, and registration fees pay for the inspections.

sections.h2: How do Royal Oak assessments and tax bills work for a seller?
sections.html:
The summer bill is due July 31 and the winter bill February 14, and postmarks are not accepted as proof of payment. A late summer bill accrues interest of one-half of 1 percent a month from August 1, and anything unpaid on March 1 goes to the Oakland County Treasurer. Owners may split the summer bill into two halves, due July 31 and October 31.

Assessed value sits at 50 percent of true cash value, while taxable value is limited by an inflation multiplier until a transfer. The Assessor's Office reviews the deed and affidavit for every transferred property, which lifts the cap. To estimate a new bill, the city suggests treating half the purchase price as taxable value, dividing by 1,000 and multiplying by the millage rate.

An owner who lived in the home before May 1 of the prior year qualifies for the Principal Residence Exemption, which the city says carries a rate about 15 mills below a non-homestead property. Appeals begin at the March Board of Review, and July and December sessions correct clerical errors and mutual mistakes. Homeowners can read their parcel records free on BS&A Online, so check yours before a buyer does.

sections.h2: What paper rules does the Oakland County recorder enforce?
sections.html:
The county examines each document before recording it, so a defect can cost weeks. Page one needs a 2.5 inch top margin and half-inch margins on every other side, and the deed must be notarized. Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 had to state the marital status of male grantors, and those signed before March 4, 2002 needed two witnesses.

  • A Sidwell Validation Unit approves the legal description before the cashier takes payment.
  • Counter hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays.
  • Copies are $1 a page, and a certified copy adds $5.

Any instrument with consideration above $99.99 is taxed, and MCL 207.523 puts the bill on the seller. The county's printed shares are $1.10 per $1,000 to the county and $7.50 per $1,000 to the state.

faqs.q: Must a Royal Oak landlord register before selling?
faqs.a: Registration is required before renting, so an occupied rental should already be registered. Hand the buyer the paperwork and ask the Building Division what the new owner files.

faqs.q: What are Royal Oak's tax due dates?
faqs.a: July 31 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill. The summer bill can be split, with the second half due October 31.

faqs.q: How does the homestead exemption change after a sale?
faqs.a: The buyer applies on the new home, and the city says it lowers the rate about 15 mills against non-homestead property. Rescind your own exemption when you sell.

faqs.q: What does the county charge to file a Royal Oak deed?
faqs.a: $30 per deed, with the $4 survey surcharge included. Warranty deeds also need a $5 tax certificate from the treasurer.

faqs.q: Does taxable value reset when I sell in Royal Oak?
faqs.a: Yes, the cap lifts for the new owner once the Assessor's Office reviews the deed and affidavit, so the buyer's bill may be higher than yours.
